1.explanation: All of the ARIA attributes and IDs that produce the invalid references are composed in these three places. ComboBox.render is where getRootProps, getInputProps and getButtonProps are combined to set aria-owns/aria-controls and aria-label on the <input> and wrapper. ListBoxField is generating the combobox role, aria-expanded, aria-owns, aria-controls and is injecting an aria-label for open/close, which conflicts with the visible <label>. And ListBoxMenu is the component that actually stamps the menu’s ID (`${id}__menu`) and role=listbox. Because these three generate the mismatched or duplicated IDs and override the label linkage, they are the right spots to update: • Ensure the menu ID is unique and matches exactly what the input/owner reference expects • Switch from aria-label to aria-labelledby (or conditionally suppress aria-label when a <label> exists) • Remove or reconcile duplicate aria-owns/controls so that DAP sees a valid ID on the referenced element.
1.bug_scenario: When running the React ComboBox examples under DAP (IBM’s accessibility testing tool), several WAI-ARIA violations appear. The menu container and the input both use aria-owns/aria-controls pointing at an ID that isn’t correctly registered on the target element, so DAP complains that “The id carbon-combobox-example__menu specified for WAI-ARIA property aria-owns, aria-controls…is not valid.” In addition, the combobox widget is given an aria-label that conflicts with its <label> element, so interactive elements are flagged as missing an accessible name, and the visible label isn’t exposed correctly.

2.explanation:
• ComboBox (ComboBox.js) is where the input and listbox get their ARIA attributes (aria-label, aria-controls, aria-owns). The render() method currently sets these IDs unconditionally and doesn’t always match an existing element, leading to invalid IDREFs.
• ListBoxField (ListBoxField.js) is responsible for the combobox container’s role, aria-owns and aria-controls. Its logic builds the menu ID as `${id}__menu`, but because it relies on the ‘aria-expanded’ prop coming from Downshift, the timing and naming sometimes misalign.
• ListBoxMenu (ListBoxMenu.js) constructs the actual menu’s id as `${id}__menu`. If ComboBox or Field ever passes the wrong `id` prop or the menu isn’t rendered yet, aria-owns/controls point at nothing.
To fix the DAP violations you’ll need to:
1. In ComboBox.render(), only emit aria-controls on the input when the menu is actually present, and ensure the `id` prop passed to ListBox.Menu matches exactly the input’s id.
2. In ListBoxField, consolidate or remove duplicate aria-owns/controls so there’s a single source of truth for the relationship, and optionally switch to aria-labelledby pointing at the visible label.
3. Confirm in ListBoxMenu that the computed `id` matches the value used by both Field and input. Adjust string concatenation if double-underscore usage conflicts with ID validation rules.
2.bug_scenario: When the React ComboBox is rendered and opened, its ARIA attributes point at an invalid menu ID, and the hidden off-screen input has no proper accessible name. In the screenshot you can see DAP complaining “The id carbon-combobox-example__menu specified for WAI-ARIA property aria-owns, aria-controls on element div is not valid,” and “An interactive element/widget must have an accessible name.” The combo’s input and its list container aren’t correctly wired up for ARIA, so assistive tools flag IDREF and naming errors.
